messages:
ida: Heads up — our q4b quant canary (deployed to canary-2) is showing a sharp drop in generation diversity compared to fp16 on the same promptset. Looks correlated with golden set shrink after last dedupe pass.

sam: ugh. which metric? perplexity or n-gram diversity?

ida: ngram-uniq@100 and distinct-2 both down ~18%. Qual evals flagging repetitive completions on conversational intents.

mike: did we change golden selection rules recently? I remember we tightened the fuzzyhash threshold.

natalie: yes — last week we de-duped anchors with simhash <= 0.92 and removed low-entropy turns. That removed ~1.2k golden candidates. I can paste the query we used.

natalie: ```sql
-- removed near-duplicates by simhash and short-turn filter
WITH candidates AS (
  SELECT id, simhash, len(prompt) AS plen, len(response) AS rlen
  FROM promptbank
  WHERE created_at < '2026-03-01'
)
DELETE FROM golden_pool
WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM candidates WHERE simhash < 0.92 OR plen < 30 OR rlen < 20);
```

sam: cool — that explains the shrink. But why is q4b quant worse than fp16? Could be quant sensitivity to repeated tokens (kv cache effects) or the holdout distribution shift post-dedupe.

ida: hypothesis: dedupe removed diverse edge anchors (long-form clarifiers) so canary sees fewer conditioning examples; quantized kernels then amplify looped tokens.

mike: propose immediate mitigations: 1) reinstate a microgolden slice of previously removed anchors (random 300) and run q4b smoke; 2) run pairwise compare (fp16 vs q4b) on the full pre-dedupe holdout; 3) add a labeler ticket to review removed anchors for semantic uniqueness.

natalie: I can restore a sample and export to curie-bot for automated A/B. Giving me 30m to produce the list.

curie-bot: Canary summary (canary-2): 2026-03-23 14:02 UTC — model=q4b-int4, traffic=1%, latency=220ms, ngram-uniq@100=0.62 (fp16 baseline=0.75), regen-rate=3.1%

ida: thanks. mike, can you spin up the A/B job and target the microgolden? Use same prompts + 3-shot variation. Keep top-k sampling consistent.

mike: on it. tagging @natalie for labeling SLA — we'll need a 48h window to vet restored anchors.

natalie: ack. will triage and flag any PII/deid issues. If labeler capacity is tight, suggest we prioritize anchors that increase token variance (len > 120 and semantic-similarity < 0.85 to existing golden).

sam: after A/B, if q4b still loses, we should try kernel fallback to int8-fast for attention and see if that helps; also test small prompt-level temp bump to break repetition.

ida: agreed. also add an eval to the benchmark dashboard that tracks "golden-recall" (how many golden anchors are covered in canary -> completion variance). That'll help catch this earlier.

mike: logging tasks: G-3471 restore microgolden sample, G-3472 run A/B job, G-3473 labeler triage ticket. I'll open them now.

natalie: opened G-3473 and assigned to labeling-ops. ETA 48h.

ida: sweet. if anyone sees similar drop on other quant variants ping here. I'll follow up with the canary A/B results once Mike posts them. :eyes:
